title: Measurement-efficient energy estimator for quantum chemistry of photodynamic materials
authors: Connor Lenihan, Kripa Panchagnula, Luca Erhart, Jem Guhit, Carlo A. Gaggioli, Gabriel Greene-Diniz, Gabriel Laude, Megan Cerys Rowe, Fabian Finger, Pranav Kalidindi, Enrico Rinaldi, Mikko Muuronen, Chandrika Mulakala, Thomas M. Soini, Elvira Shishenina, David Muñoz Ramo, David Zsolt Manrique
abstract: Accurate modelling of chemical reaction rates requires precise correlated energy differences. Quantum computing offers a potential route to their determination, but extracting energies from quantum-prepared states can demand prohibitive sampling. We demonstrate measurement-efficient correlated energy estimation using an electronically challenging H$_2$DBB--Ru model derived from a Ru-functionalized hafnium metal-organic framework relevant to radiodynamic and photodynamic therapies. The mixed estimator combines a quantum-prepared target with sparse multiconfiguration references and recovers ground-state corrections using magnitude-only compute-uncompute measurements. Analytical variance estimates predict 1.6 mHa precision with a few hundred shots, about 100 times fewer than the single-determinant formulation and three orders of magnitude fewer than optimized Hamiltonian-term sampling. With approximate targets, it reaches comparable accuracy using simpler state preparation than direct expectation-value estimation. Emulator and trapped-ion experiments on Quantinuum Helios validate the approach up to (10,10), including a 50-qubit circuit combining AI-assisted state preparation with error detection, providing a measurement-efficient route to correlated energy differences for challenging chemical problems.
summary: This paper introduces a measurement-efficient mixed estimator to calculate correlated energy differences for challenging quantum chemistry problems relevant to photodynamic materials. By combining quantum-prepared target states with classical references, the method drastically reduces the required quantum measurement shots compared to standard techniques. The approach is validated on a complex molecular model and tested on trapped-ion quantum hardware.
main_problem: Accurately determining correlated energy differences for quantum chemistry, which is crucial for modeling chemical reaction rates in photodynamic and radiodynamic therapies.
main_result: The proposed mixed estimator achieves predicted precision of 1.6 mHa with significantly fewer quantum shots compared to single-determinant or Hamiltonian-term sampling methods.
method: The authors developed and applied a measurement-efficient mixed estimator (EME) that combines a quantum-prepared target state with sparse multiconfiguration references to estimate electronic energies.
model_or_system: The study uses the H2DBB--Ru molecular model, derived from a Ru-functionalized hafnium metal-organic framework, which serves as a challenging benchmark for electronic structure calculations.
key_observables: Electronic energy differences (activation energy, $\Delta E$), overlap terms ($\langle\Psi|\Lambdaangle$, $\langle\Psi|\Phiangle$), and required quantum circuit resources (qubit count, depth).
important_parameters: Target precision of 1.6 mHa; comparison across active spaces up to (10,10); comparison against CASCI benchmarks.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the ability to classically obtain the reference state $|\Phiangle$ and resolves sign ambiguities by assuming the target state is the ground state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the end-to-end workflow, integrating classical calculations, quantum state preparation (pp-tUPS/sMCS), direct overlap measurements, and the final mixed estimator calculation.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical formulation of the mixed estimator, benchmarks it against established quantum chemistry methods using the H2DBB--Ru system, and validates the approach using both emulator and trapped-ion experiments on Quantinuum Helios.
why_interesting: The development of measurement-efficient estimators directly addresses the resource bottleneck in applying quantum computing to complex molecular simulations, bridging quantum information theory with physical chemistry.

Figure 3 compares the direct expectation value and the mixed estimator using the same sequence of approximate target states for all three active spaces. For pp-tUPS, two layers place both estimators within the ±1.6 mHa interval for both geometries. For sMCS, the mixed estimator generally approaches the CASCI energies with fewer retained determinants than the direct expectation value, with the clearest separation in the larger ASs. Because the state is not exact in this test and the mixed estimator is non-variational, it is not guaranteed to converge monotonically or to be closer at every truncation.
